newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says he will continue to govern.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says he will continue to govern.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed on Thursday to stay in power despite police recommendations he be indicted in a corruption scandal.

"This government is not going anywhere. We are not going anywhere. We are staying where the people and history have put us," Netanyahu said in a speech to activists of his Likud party, in his first remarks since the police recommendation was made public.

"I have come to tell you today that we will continue to lead the state of Israel...We will continue on this path until the year 2000 and I tell you, beyond the year 2000," Netanyahu said after hundreds of activists gave him a standing ovation and shouted "Bibi, King of Israel".

As Netanyahu spoke, Israeli prosecutors met at a secluded location near Jerusalem to decide whether to accept the police recommendations he be charged with fraud and breach of trust in connection with the appointment of an attorney general.

"I am convinced the truth will triumph," said Netanyahu, who has vehemently denied the allegations of influence-peddling. He said his office had been inundated with supportive phone calls from the public.
Netanyahu smiled broadly at the crowd and gave them a "thumbs-up" sign before starting his brief speech.
